WHAT THIS WORK DOES

Review the evidence before making the call.

Each proposed tool call is compared with prior approved and blocked actions. Unfamiliar cases can be escalated to a person, and their decision becomes evidence for the next check.

Offline-first desktop engineering

04

The backbone of
campus commerce.

Our campus credit system, built from scratch, supports more than US$1.2 million in annual purchases. OneTap Vendor and the SU app form a backbone of everyday life at BITS Pilani: vendors scan a student’s QR, purchases reach their mess account, and balances are billed at semester end.

WHAT THIS WORK DOES

US$1.2M+ in annual campus purchases. One connected credit system.

Together, the SU app and OneTap Vendor support 5,000+ students across BITS Pilani. The QR in the SU app connects vendors to a student’s mess account, making everyday campus purchases possible on credit and settling those charges at semester end.

Open to a conversation

A few things,
before we talk.

What I’m working toward, how I build, and where to reach me.

A good question is a good place to start.

I’m looking for software and AI engineering roles or internships, especially where I can work on useful AI applications, real-time systems, or products with real users.

I start with the user’s workflow and the constraints: timing for voice systems, evidence for agents, connectivity for campus billing. Then I build a small end-to-end path, test the difficult parts, and work toward a dependable release.

I’m pursuing a B.E. in Mathematics & Computing at BITS Pilani, with graduation expected in May 2028. I also lead the Students’ Union Technical Team, a team of 20 student engineers.

Each project has a case study explaining the implementation and its tradeoffs. Public repositories are on GitHub. Technical previews and prototypes include their current limitations; generated interface concepts are labelled.
